doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Learning piano chords and playing church drums
summary: Turner shows him chords on the piano and he starts on snare and bass drum in the small, poor congregation after the Crash.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What were some of things that he taught you - say, on the piano?

Well, I can remember he made a kind of a sound like a rink, tink, rink, tink, boom, boom, boom -- I'm singing this, like, that's the way it sounded. And he showed me how to chord in B flat, E flat. He would sit me on his lap and spread my fingers out on the keys, but like I said, there was a whole lot of music around that house.
When did you begin to play in the church?

Oh, let's see ... I was about 8 or 9 years old. And Reverend Turner had drums, too; just a snare drum and a bass drum -- with a pedal and sticks, and he told me how to beat them. And I don't know -- it came kind of natural, you might say,

So I began playing the drums in the church. By then, the church had broke up -- this had to be around 1930 -- the church was small and the congregation was small; everybody was very poor. I think they lost the big church they had with the Crash, because they had to take smaller living quarters, and like I said, I was staying with Mr. and Mrs. Turner at that time.

And I was playing. In church, we had a piano player, Mrs. Phillips, and Billy Johnson played great cymbals. We didn't have no horns, or at least I didn't see no horns over at their house -- just people clapping their hands, and
tambourines and singing. But it was a beautiful feeling -- a beautiful feeling. And that started me off.
